This site documents the analysis behind
[*immgenT: A Comprehensive Reference of Convergent T-cell States in the Mouse*](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.01.30.702892v3):
an atlas of over 700,000 mouse T cells from more than 700 samples across 80 experiments,
profiled by single-cell RNA-seq, 128-plex CITE-seq and paired αβ TCR
sequencing, and organised into eight lineages and 107 reproducible clusters.

Each page below covers one published figure. For every panel it shows the R
code that produced it, the panel itself, and a caption stating what it shows.

## Main figures

+ [Figure 1: Scope of the immgenT Open Source Project](Figure1.html)
+ [Figure 2: immgenT harmonizes T-cell representation across experiments and delineates major T-cell lineages](Figure2.html)
+ [Figure 3: Reference MDE plot for each T-cell lineage](Figure3.html)
+ [Figure 4: 107 immgenT consensus clusters preserve heterogeneity and enhance biological interpretability](Figure4.html)
+ [Figure 5: T-RBI integrates external datasets into the immgenT framework](Figure5.html)
+ [Figure 6: Reuse and redistribution of shared T-cell states across tissues and immune perturbations](Figure6.html)
+ [Figure 7: Effector gene expression across T-cell states](Figure7.html)
+ [Figure 8: Transcription factor expression across T-cell states](Figure8.html)
+ [Figure 10: AI-based reference mapping reveals the limits of marker- and signature-defined T-cell identity](Figure10.html)

**Figure 9** (T-cell states are defined by combinations of gene programs) is
produced by the gene-program factorization analysis, which has its own
repository and site:
[immgenT-GP-analysis](https://aguerozz.github.io/immgenT-GP-analysis/).

**Figure 11** is the correspondence table between immgenT clusters and
previously published subset names. It is a table typeset for the manuscript,
not a plot, and is distributed with the paper as Extended Data.

## Reproducing these figures

Every page above is generated by a single R script in
[`script/`](https://github.com/dzemmour/immgenT-cosmo-paper/tree/main/script),
which sources shared plotting and data-loading helpers from
[`code/R/`](https://github.com/dzemmour/immgenT-cosmo-paper/tree/main/code/R).
To regenerate a figure, run from the repository root:

```
Rscript script/Figure4.R
```

Panels are written as one PDF per panel into `figures/<figure>/`. The pages on
this site display PNGs converted from those PDFs by
`Rscript script/render_site_assets.R`, so the site cannot drift from the panel
set the scripts produced; the code shown on each page is displayed, not
re-executed when the site is built.

The input data (~3.9 GB of Seurat objects and cached intermediates) is not in
this repository. It is deposited on Zenodo as `immgenT-Cosmo.zip`:

+ <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21839963>

Unpack it at the repository root, so that `data/` sits next to `script/` and
`analysis/`; the scripts read `data/` as a relative path and are run from the
repository root. `code/README.md` lists every file, what reads it, and where it
comes from.
